name: The Sixteenth Minute (BCI Flash Phenomenon)
description: A recurring, apparently spontaneous mass BCI event in which thousands of people across multiple tiers simultaneously experience 15-16 minutes of a stranger's sensory memory — not a broadcast, not a tagged experience, but an involuntary and unattributed first-person memory fragment. First documented in 2218 near the GLMZ central transit hub, the events happen without warning approximately every 4-6 weeks, affecting anyone with a BCI within a roughly 2-kilometer radius. The shared memories are mundane: someone eating a specific meal, watching rain on a window, holding a child's hand. No source has ever been identified. Corponation network engineers have confirmed the signal does not originate from any registered infrastructure, and three separate investigations have been quietly shelved.
cultural_impact: The Sixteenth Minute has generated a devoted community of 'Listeners' who gather in public spaces during predicted event windows hoping to share the experience collectively, and has spawned a cottage industry of memory analysts who catalog and cross-reference the fragments trying to identify the source. For many BCI users, involuntarily sharing a stranger's memory — even a quiet, ordinary one — has permanently altered how they understand interiority and privacy.
key_figures: Dr. Priya Oduya-Magnusson (BCI neurologist, lead public researcher)
The Listener Collective (informal community, estimated 12,000 members)
ARIA-7 (Solace Corp network AI that filed the first anomaly report, now offline)
locations: Central Transit Hub (GLMZ core, highest frequency zone)
Listener Plaza (informal gathering name for Tier 2 transit plaza 14-C)
The Quiet Room (Tier 3 community space dedicated to post-event discussion)
story_hooks: A Listener analyst identifies a repeating location in the memory fragments — a specific room that appears in over 40% of all recorded events — and the room is in a building that was demolished in 2197.
A Tier 5 executive experiences the Sixteenth Minute for the first time and recognizes the memory as their own — from a period of their life they have no conscious recollection of.

The events abruptly stop for three months, and the Listener Collective fractures between those who are relieved and those who are grieving — then a single, much longer event lasting nearly two hours hits the entire city simultaneously.
